discovery: Individually trapped neutral atoms in optical tweezers and Rydberg-blockade entanglement, establishing programmable atom arrays for quantum simulation and computation

nominees.name: Philippe Grangier
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum optics
motivation: Grangier first trapped and imaged single neutral atoms in microscopic optical tweezers (2001) and, with Browaeys, demonstrated Rydberg blockade and entanglement between two individually addressed atoms (2009-2010). Browaeys then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms, making them clean quantum simulators of spin models. Lukin proposed the dipole-blockade mechanism for neutral-atom quantum gates (2000-2001) and led the development of large-scale programmable Rydberg arrays, observing new quantum phases, quantum many-body scars and, recently, logical qubits with error correction. Together they turned the control of single atoms and their entanglement, once a gedankenexperiment, into a platform with hundreds to thousands of qubits. This is one of the most striking achievements of the second quantum revolution: foundational questions about individual quantum systems are now answered and used every day in laboratories and emerging technologies.
